title: Ada and the Uniform
premise: In 1912, Beatrix Fairweather has spent a decade as driver and unofficial censor for Lady Constance Hale, a prominent suffragist, quietly reading and sometimes destroying letters to protect the movement's fragile alliances. When a sealed letter arrives naming the Ashcombe family—patrons whose daughter, Ada, serves as a uniformed nurse—as targets of a government smear meant to discredit the suffrage cause, Beatrix must decide whether to break her own rule of silence. Racing against a dawn tide and the victors' version of history, she smuggles testimony, letters, and Ada herself aboard a ship bound for safety, getting the truth on the record at the cost of her invisibility, her position, and nearly her freedom.
about_author: Tamsin Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing suffragette correspondence in provincial English collections. She writes historical fiction about the women history filed under 'assistant.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Things
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A day in her careful routine: driving Lady Constance, steaming open letters, deciding which silences to keep. She prides herself on being unreadable. The emotional beat is quiet competence masking loneliness—until a sealed letter with a government frank arrives that she cannot bring herself to open.

chapters.title: Ada in Grey
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The letter names the Ashcombes as targets of a fabricated scandal tied to their suffrage donations. Their daughter Ada, in her VAD nurse's uniform, arrives at the house asking Lady Constance for help her mother doesn't know she needs. Beatrix recognizes a fellow keeper of silences—and feels the first crack in hers.

chapters.title: What the Lady Doesn't Ask
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Lady Constance, wary of political ruin, hesitates; Beatrix hides the letter's existence and begins her own investigation through the letters she's archived for ten years. Emotional beat: the intoxicating, frightening discovery that her secret knowledge is power, not just burden.

chapters.title: The Archive Under the Stairs
chapters.summary: Beatrix and Ada's POV, alternating. In the cellar archive, Beatrix shows Ada a decade of evidence—letters proving the smear is orchestrated by a Home Office clerk. Ada reveals the Ashcombes' solicitor has already been bought. The beat is two invisible women becoming conspirators.

chapters.title: A Man Who Counts Letters
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The clerk's agent appears at the house, offering Beatrix money for the correspondence. She plays dumb, but realizes they know someone inside has read too much. Emotional beat: fear curdling into defiance; the price of survival is rising.

chapters.title: Tide Tables
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada learns the Ashcombes intend to send her abroad to keep her quiet and compliant, sailing on the morning tide. She and Beatrix plan to turn exile into escape with evidence aboard—testimony that must reach a sympathetic barrister before the ship sails or the papers are seized.

chapters.title: Constance, Woken
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix finally confesses ten years of reading, altering, and destroying letters to Lady Constance. The betrayal is real—but so is the proof that Beatrix's silences once saved the movement. Emotional beat: rupture and grudging alliance; justice outside the law requires trust inside the house.

chapters.title: Night of the Copyists
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. In one long night, the household women copy the archive by lamplight—maids, typists, Ada in her uniform as disguise. The agent circles the house. Rising tension: they finish at 4 a.m., but the agent has bought the night porter.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Beatrix and Ada's POV. At the docks, the agent confronts them; Beatrix trades her silence—her ten years of secrets, including ones that could ruin Lady Constance—for safe passage of the evidence and Ada. Climax: she chooses the record over her own protection, boarding with the satchel as the gangway rises.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, months later. The barrister's affidavit lands; the clerk resigns; the Ashcombe name is cleared, though the papers credit 'anonymous correspondents.' Beatrix, dismissed and unregretful, opens a small typing office—her name on the door at last. Final beat: belonging earned not by invisibility, but by testimony.
